provenance: Synthetic teaching examples, not measured MySQL telemetry.
generation_policy: Fixed independent seeds and predefined incidents; no estimator fitting or score-based selection.

metric_definitions.queries_per_second: queries/second during the one-minute sampling interval
metric_definitions.response_time_ms: synthetic probe round-trip latency in milliseconds
metric_definitions.slow_queries: slow-query count during this interval, not a cumulative counter
metric_definitions.connection_errors: failed-connection count during this interval, not a cumulative counter

scenarios.MAD.csv: Stable baseline with isolated high and low QPS values; other metrics unchanged.
scenarios.Isolation_Forest.csv: Three normal load profiles and rare simultaneous extremes in five metrics.
scenarios.LOF.csv: Dense and sparse normal clusters; incidents lie just outside the dense cluster, within overall marginal ranges.
scenarios.One_Class_SVM.csv: QPS and connections follow latent load t; latency follows 15+3*t^2. Incidents combine middle QPS/connections with high latency.

limitations: Filenames identify intended teaching concepts, not exclusive algorithm compatibility or guaranteed superiority.
All four algorithms can be evaluated on every file using the same held-out rows.
Synthetic results cannot establish accuracy on production workloads.
Use all five metrics in DBMS mode; a one-metric CSV run loses relational information.
The operational noise guard may suppress local and relational anomalies; disable it to examine raw algorithms.
One percent contamination/nu does not guarantee one percent test alerts. Fifteen injected events occupy five percent of test rows.
Event counts intentionally remain zero in the MAD, LOF and One-Class SVM baselines.
